hood_desc: A southern district around the Quba Mosque, the first mosque in Islam, residential and green; suits pilgrims wanting to combine ziyarat visits with a calmer stay outside the crush of the Haram.

A central district near the old Hejaz Railway station and within walking reach of the Prophet's Mosque, dense with hotels and eateries; suits pilgrims wanting proximity to the Haram on a mid-range budget.
A modern, upscale western district with newer hotels, malls and wide roads, farther from the Haram; suits pilgrims and families with a car who prefer newer, comfortable lodging.
A residential area near Masjid al-Qiblatayn and battlefield ziyarat sites, a moderate distance from the Haram; suits pilgrims focused on visiting historic sites and quieter surroundings.
The innermost ring directly around the Prophet's Mosque, wall-to-wall pilgrim hotels and shops, walkable to prayers; suits pilgrims who want to step straight into the Haram, at premium prices.

water.note: Treated water meets standards, but bottled water is commonly preferred due to plumbing and taste.

transit.pay: Download the Madinah Bus app to register and load a prepaid card/QR code, since cash isn't used onboard; SAPTCO also handles intercity bookings to Makkah and Jeddah. Local rides are inexpensive, roughly SAR 2-4 (~$0.55-1.10) per trip.
transit.note: Medina has minimal tourist-oriented transit - most visitors walk within the Haram area or use taxis/Uber for longer trips.

landmarks: Al-Masjid an-Nabawi (Prophet's Mosque)
Islam's second-holiest site, famous for its iconic Green Dome and vast marble courtyards.
Quba Mosque
The first mosque built in Islamic history, notable for its elegant white domes and minarets.
Masjid al-Qiblatain (Mosque of the Two Qiblas)
Historic mosque marking the site where the direction of prayer was changed, with a distinctive twin-mihrab design.
Mount Uhud
A dramatic reddish mountain and site of a pivotal early Islamic battle, offering striking desert-mountain scenery.
Al-Baqi Cemetery
One of Islam's oldest and most revered cemeteries, adjacent to the Prophet's Mosque, with rows of simple domed graves.
Seven Mosques (Masajid al-Sab'ah)
A cluster of small historic mosques marking the site of the Battle of the Trench, notable for their preserved fortification-era architecture.
Masjid al-Ghamama
One of the oldest mosques in Medina, built where the Prophet is said to have prayed for rain, recognizable by its Ottoman-style stonework.
King Fahd Complex for Printing the Holy Quran
A monumental modern complex known for its grand entrance and gardens, symbolizing Medina's role in Quranic publishing.
Hejaz Railway Museum (Al-Madinah Station)
A beautifully preserved Ottoman-era railway station showcasing historic locomotives and Islamic-Ottoman architecture.
Dar Al Madinah Museum
A museum dedicated to the history and heritage of Medina, offering insight into the city's Islamic past through artifacts and exhibits.

train.note: No international trains. The Haramain High Speed Railway links Madinah with Jeddah (and King Abdulaziz Airport), King Abdullah Economic City and Makkah at up to 300 km/h from the Madinah HHR station north-west of the centre. Note that Madinah's central holy district is open to Muslims only.

intl.to: Egypt, the UAE, Bahrain & other Arab countries (SAPTCO network)

bus.note: SAPTCO is the national coach company and runs both domestic services from Madinah and an international network to neighbouring Arab countries, though most cross-border departures are routed via Jeddah or Riyadh - check whether your route starts in Madinah. Bring your passport and confirm visa rules; non-Muslims cannot enter central Madinah.

ferry.note: Madinah is inland and has no port. The nearest sea crossings are on the Red Sea coast at Yanbu and Jeddah, from where ferries to Egypt (e.g. towards Suez/Safaga) run intermittently - reach them by road or by the high-speed train to Jeddah first.
